defects.what: The baseline schema this seed is written against does not exist in the repo, so the file cannot be applied and every ON CONFLICT / type-cast claim in its header is verified only against a DDL source the archive README says is NOT what ships.
defects.evidence: `ls /home/user/dikagustiana.com/supabase/migrations/` returns exactly two entries: `20260731235900_seed_surviving_content.sql` and `_archive/`. `find /home/user/dikagustiana.com -name '*baseline*'` returns nothing, yet `_archive/README.md:7` promises `../20260731*_baseline_schema.sql`. Executed against an empty database (what `supabase db push` does on the fresh project today): `psql:seed.sql:139: ERROR: relation "public.sections" does not exist` — it dies on the first statement. The header block at lines 93-107 asserts each ON CONFLICT "names a real unique constraint" in "the baseline schema"; those names can only be checked against `_archive`, which `README.md:4-7` states is "not applied to the current project and must never be replayed". Three concrete dependencies the seed hard-codes and cannot verify: `'draft'::public.content_status_enum` (lines 461, 543, 589) and `'published'::public.content_status_enum` (line 678) require the enum from `_archive/20260204074340_*.sql:3` to survive verbatim in the baseline; `finance_modules.module_meta` (lines 249+, 281+, 344+, 386+) exists only because of ALTERs in `_archive/20260219_001_*.sql:22` and `_archive/20260220_001_*.sql:82`; `essays.section` (every essay INSERT column list) is a column `_archive/20260215_001_*.sql:11` lists as step 6 "Drop essays.section column" of its own plan. The author's ordering claim ("20260731235900 ... sorts after any 20260731* baseline") is likewise unverifiable and false if the baseline lands later in the day.
defects.fix: Land the baseline migration first, then re-run this seed against it and re-confirm the 7 constraint names, the two enum casts, `finance_modules.module_meta`, and `essays.section` against the real DDL rather than against `_archive`. Also confirm the baseline's timestamp is < 235900. The seed's data does not need to change — the verification does.

defects.what: Replay aborts hard if any finance track ever holds two modules at the same sort_order. The three module_id lookups are scalar subqueries on (track_slug, sort_order), but nothing in the schema or the app keeps that pair unique — so the file is not idempotent in exactly the scenario its own assertion thresholds were written to tolerate.
defects.evidence: Lines 456-457, 538-539, 584-585: `(SELECT m.id FROM public.finance_modules m WHERE m.track_slug = '<track>' AND m.sort_order = v.module_no)`. `finance_modules` carries only `UNIQUE (slug)` — `_archive/20260218_001_finance_modules_and_slug_unification.sql:56` and `_archive/20260220_001_fix_production_finance_data.sql:26`; confirmed in the live test DB, `pg_constraint` shows `finance_modules_slug_key | UNIQUE (slug)` and nothing on `(track_slug, sort_order)`. Meanwhile `src/pages/FinanceWorkspace.tsx:362-379` hands the admin a free-text integer `sort_order` field on every module and writes it with `.update({ title, thesis, sort_order: parsedSortOrder, framing_content })` — validating only `Number.isNaN`, never uniqueness. Executed: after `INSERT INTO finance_modules(track_slug,slug,title,sort_order) VALUES ('analytics','owner-added-module','Owner Added',5);` a replay of the seed died with `psql:/tmp/pgt/seed.sql:625: ERROR: more than one row returned by a subquery used as an expression` — even though `ON CONFLICT (slug) DO NOTHING` means not one row would have been written (rollback was clean: essays stayed 106). This contradicts the file's own design: the assertions at lines 711-718 deliberately use `>=` because "later admin rows could legitimately raise them".
defects.fix: Make the lookup total instead of assuming uniqueness: add `ORDER BY m.id LIMIT 1` to each of the three subqueries at lines 456-457, 538-539, 584-585 — or, better, resolve `module_id` from the module's globally-unique `slug` by carrying the module slug in the VALUES list alongside `module_no`, so the lookup keys on the one column the schema actually constrains.

defects.what: The finance_sections DO UPDATE silently reverts admin edits on replay — the exact policy the file explicitly refuses to apply to finance_settings, and its stated justification for the fsli_pages DO NOTHING is backwards.
defects.evidence: Lines 225-229: `ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET title = EXCLUDED.title, description = EXCLUDED.description, icon = EXCLUDED.icon, sort_order = EXCLUDED.sort_order`. `src/hooks/queries/useFinance.ts:51-65` (`useUpdateFinanceSection`) UPDATEs `finance_sections` with exactly `{ title?, description?, sort_order? }` — three of those four columns. So a second run of this file silently discards the owner's Finance Workspace edits to all four finance tracks. The file's own rule at lines 101-103 is the opposite: "finance_settings ... DO NOTHING — DO UPDATE would reset a featured_finance_essay_id the owner had since set." And the justification given for the fsli_pages DO NOTHING at lines 164-165 ("the figures are editable from the admin UI and must not be reset by a re-run") is factually inverted: grep across `src/` shows `fsli_pages` has no UPDATE or UPSERT path at all — only SELECT (`useFsliPages.ts:23,38`, `useUnifiedContent.ts:93,142`) and DELETE (`useUnifiedContent.ts:290`). The one seeded table that is genuinely admin-editable is the one that got the clobbering clause.
defects.fix: Change line 225 to `ON CONFLICT (slug) DO NOTHING`. The fresh baseline has no finance_sections rows, so the 4-row end state still lands intact on the first run and convergence costs nothing; if `icon` genuinely must converge (it is the one column the admin UI cannot write), narrow the DO UPDATE to `icon = EXCLUDED.icon` only.

defects.evidence: Candidate line 147: "We deliberately do NOT reuse either" (the fixed UUID plus the column DEFAULT from `20260219_004`). But `/home/user/dikagustiana.com/supabase/seed.sql:63-66` inserts `seed-published-essay` omitting `category_id`, and `essays.category_id` is NOT NULL (`_archive/20260215_001_enforce_category_hierarchy.sql:103`) with FK RESTRICT (:122-123). The only thing that made that fixture insert work in the lost project was `_archive/20260219_004_seed_fundamentals_lessons.sql:11-21` — the pinned category row plus `ALTER COLUMN category_id SET DEFAULT '0f111111-...'`. Tested both baseline variants after applying the candidate: (A) baseline carries the DEFAULT → `ERROR: insert or update on table "essays" violates foreign key constraint "essays_category_id_fkey" DETAIL: Key (category_id)=(0f111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111) is not present in table "categories".` (B) baseline drops the DEFAULT → `ERROR: null value in column "category_id" of relation "essays" violates not-null constraint`. `scripts/setup-test-db.sh` runs `npx supabase db reset` (migrations + seed); `docs/e2e-live-testing.md:27` and :51-53 document the same path.
defects.fix: Pin the id in section 2 while keeping the subquery resolution everywhere else: `INSERT INTO public.categories (id, name, slug, section_id, sort_order) SELECT '0f111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'::uuid, 'General', 'finance-general', s.id, 0 FROM public.sections s WHERE s.slug = 'finance' ON CONFLICT (section_id, slug) DO NOTHING;`. This costs nothing (essays still resolve `category_id` by subquery, so it still works if the row pre-exists under another id) and makes `db reset` complete on a fresh database.

defects.what: The `n <> 105` curriculum-stub assertion uses exact equality on a slug pattern the file does not exclusively own, so any re-run after the owner adds one more lesson aborts the whole seed.
defects.evidence: Line 723: `IF n <> 105 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'seed: expected 105 curriculum stubs, found %', n; END IF;` counting `WHERE slug ~ '^(sf|pf|fa)-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$'`. Demonstrated: after inserting `sf-13-04` (a legitimate 4th lesson in strategic-finance module 13, exactly the kind of row the header expects the admin UI to add), re-applying the file gives `ERROR: seed: expected 105 curriculum stubs, found 106` at file line 768 and rolls back everything. This contradicts the file's own stated rule that exact equality is used "only for the closed sets this file owns" — this set is not closed.
defects.fix: Either scope the count to the 105 slugs this file writes (`AND slug IN (...)`, or join against the VALUES list) or relax the threshold to `IF n < 105` to match the other counters.

defects.what: module_id is resolved with a scalar subquery on (track_slug, sort_order), a pair with no uniqueness guarantee, so a re-run aborts if a module with a duplicate sort_order is ever added to a track.
defects.evidence: `_archive/20260218_001_finance_modules_and_slug_unification.sql:53-64` defines `finance_modules` with only `slug text NOT NULL UNIQUE`; confirmed on the live test DB — `pg_constraint` for `public.finance_modules` lists only `finance_modules_pkey`, `finance_modules_slug_key`, `finance_modules_track_slug_fkey`. No UNIQUE(track_slug, sort_order). Demonstrated: after `INSERT INTO public.finance_modules (track_slug, slug, sort_order, title) VALUES ('planning','treasury-architecture-ii',4,'Treasury Architecture II');`, re-applying the file gives `ERROR: more than one row returned by a subquery used as an expression` at file line 577 — before the assertions can produce a diagnostic message.
defects.fix: Add `ORDER BY m.created_at LIMIT 1` (or `m.slug`) to each of the three module lookup subqueries so the resolution stays deterministic, and let the existing per-track/per-module assertions catch a genuine mismatch with a readable error.

defects.what: Provenance comment states the stubs' sort_order is NULL; it is 0.
defects.evidence: Line 447: "finance_section and sort_order are left NULL exactly as the originals left them". `essays.sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0` (`_archive/20251223120457_...sql:72`). Measured after apply: of the 105 stubs, `sort_order IS NULL` = 0 and `sort_order = 0` = 105 (`finance_section IS NULL` = 105, so that half of the sentence is correct). Behaviour matches the originals, which also omitted the column — only the documented claim is wrong, in a file whose value rests on its provenance notes being exact.
defects.fix: Change the comment to "finance_section is left NULL and sort_order takes its column default of 0, exactly as the originals left them".

defects.what: The published placeholder is reachable only by typing its URL — no index, track page, module list, or featured slot can surface it — so the second of the two reasons the file gives for creating it is not achieved.
defects.evidence: File lines ~648-652 justify the row partly because "a visitor arriving at a suddenly-empty site deserves an explanation." But the row is inserted with `module_id` and `finance_section` unset (INSERT column list at line 662-664 omits both) and `featured_finance_essay_id` is seeded NULL. The three queries that could list it all filter on exactly those: `useFinanceSectionEssays` uses `.eq('finance_section', dbKey)` (src/hooks/queries/useFinance.ts:161), module lesson lists use `.eq('module_id', mod.id)` (:252, :259), and `useFeaturedFinanceEssay` uses `.eq('id', settings.value)` (:125). `FinanceEssayPage` does find it by slug alone (src/pages/FinanceEssayPage.tsx:70-75), so the acceptance-bar reason (a) does hold — it is only reason (b) that fails.
defects.fix: After the essay INSERT, point the setting at it — `UPDATE public.finance_settings SET value = (SELECT id::text FROM public.essays WHERE slug = 'site-rebuild-note') WHERE key = 'featured_finance_essay_id';` — or drop reason (b) from the comment and keep the row purely as the published-read test fixture.
